correctness.rationale: All 32767 nonzero binary quartics are exhaustively partitioned into 279 orbits under 168 exact projective transformations. Each orbit representative is tested for geometric smoothness over the algebraic closure using the unit-ideal test by exact Groebner bases on all three projective charts, yielding 78 smooth orbits totaling 10920 equations. For each smooth representative, seven rational points, their formal gradient tangent lines and all seven rational line intersections are counted exactly; orbit-weighted counts give four joint categories 2040/616/1848/6416. Independent direct traversal of all 10920 smooth equations with two distinct literal coefficient/partial-derivative evaluation implementations reproduces the incidence counts, point distributions and explicit opposing nonimplication witnesses. The included copied executable was run successfully; no extrapolation, numerical approximation or unbounded logical inference is invoked.

value.rationale: Tangent filling is an established natural dual-incidence property of smooth curves. The complete first nontrivial small-field genus-three conditional probability and full cross-tabulation with the independent primal blocking property resolve a meaningful finite classification. The 616 tangent-filling nonblocking and 1848 blocking nontangent-filling curves demonstrate neither property controls the other; the number of rational points fails to determine tangent filling. Counts require nontrivial geometric smoothness certification and derivative-sensitive exact incidence, are not point-count table recomputation, and provide a reproducible benchmark for duality-based finite geometry. Scope is expressly confined to quartics over F2.
